newsitem.title: JAPAN: Compaq plans ambitious push in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Compaq plans ambitious push in Japan.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp., the world's largest seller of personal computers, said Thursday it plans an ambitious push to increase its market share in Japan where it has been struggling to compete.
It said it will increase its work force by nearly 40 percent at its Japanese unit by the end of the year in a bid to inject some energy into its business here.

"We want to hire 120 new workers this year. A little over 60 in our marketing section and about 50 more mainly in technical service," Kuniaki Fujimoto, president of Compaq's Japanese unit, Compaq KK, told Reuters in a recent interview.
Fujimoto said the planned hirings -- the firm currently has 315 employees -- reflect the firm's desire to boost revenues and profits, but he declined to provide specific target figures.

Compaq, which has captured more than 11 percent of the global PC market, has struggled to duplicate that success in Japan, where last year it ranked seventh with 3 percent of the market, down one percentage point from 1995.

When Compaq first entered Japan in 1992 with its PCs, it created the so-called "Compaq Shock," and triggered fierce price competition with its low-priced PCs costing about 50 percent less than those offered by Japanese competitors.
But it failed to to make much of a dent, trailing far behind top seller NEC Corp., which had a 33 percent market share in 1996, and No. 2 Fujitsu Ltd., with 22 percent.
